page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by a KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, delivering 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system features 48.0 GiB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio with 2.0 GiB per thread. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 (AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI), AES, FMA, BMI2, and ADX extensions. This configuration does not include local ephemeral SSD storage or bundled GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Performance testing reflects a contrast between single-core throughput and parallel execution capabilities. Single-threaded metrics fall into lower percentiles, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1313.3 and a gzip compression speed of 22.86 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded operations maintain consistent mid-range results, achieving a stress-ng multi-core benchmark of 21007.3 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8967.0. Memory bandwidth tests yield uncached read speeds of 108.94 GB/sec and write speeds of 47.99 GB/sec across large blocks. Specialized workload benchmarks show moderate performance, including a PassMark CPU rating of 21643.62, software compilation throughput of 17481.0 in Clang, and Redis SET throughput reaching 20.09 million operations per second.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU design prioritizes compute capacity over RAM volume, providing cost efficiency for processing-heavy applications that do not demand large in-memory data structures. The primary performance tradeoff lies in modest single-core execution speeds, which are offset by aggregate multi-threading performance across 24 logical processors. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is suited for multi-threaded software compilation, static web backend serving, batch processing pipelines, continuous integration systems, and microservices.
